Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The national identity card is accepted for Know Your Customer (KYC) processes in banking and financial services. Banks and non-bank financial institutions (45,000 accounts per the World Bank diagnostic) require KYC using ID documents including the CNI. However, there is no digital KYC infrastructure; verification is manual/physical only. Mobile money (Orange) also uses ID for registration.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Law No. 24.001 on the Protection of Personal Data was enacted in January 2024. The law establishes comprehensive data protection principles (lawfulness, transparency, purpose limitation, storage limitation), regulates sensitive data including biometric data, provides data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure), and requires a Data Protection Officer. It mandates the creation of an independent supervisory authority within 12 months of enactment.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: Partial oversight. The Directorate General of Public Procurement (under the Ministry of Finance and Budget) formally objected in 2018 to the Al-Madina contract for non-compliance with procurement laws. The Finance Law sets the official CNI price at CFA 4,500. However, revenues from ID card issuance have reportedly not been appearing in the state budget, suggesting limited effective financial control over the ID system.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Identity documents are accepted but not mandatory for healthcare access. The Ministry of Health uses identity for records, and hospitals issue birth attestations (55% of births occur in health facilities). Health services are generally accessible without strict ID requirements given the humanitarian context. No evidence of mandatory ID-linked healthcare access found.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration with ID is accepted (not mandatory in the strictest enforcement sense but required by regulation). Decision 018/MPTNT/CMAJ/09 (2009) required SIM card registration with a valid ID. A 2017 decision mandated inactivation of unregistered SIMs. The World Bank noted 1.185 million subscribers with 20–30% churn and high verification costs. Non-biometric ID registration applies.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: Identity documents are accepted (not universally mandatory) for social services. The Ministry of Social Affairs and National Reconciliation (MASRN) and humanitarian agencies (WFP, UNICEF) use identity for beneficiary identification in cash transfer and social protection programs. The World Bank ID4D diagnostic noted social protection programs (PACAD, LONDO) covering 190,000 and 35,500 beneficiaries respectively. The lack of widespread ID coverage is a key barrier to inclusive social protection delivery.
